story.title: THE COMET'S SECOND TAIL
story.deck: A comet grows a tail that walks upwind, nine thousand young shells of living plasma sit across the grain lane, and a claim holder keeps the key to a sweep that would sterilize them.
story.shape: Interplanetary corridor crisis in six scenes: the ecology declines both offered paths, chooses a third, and has to be met at its own pace; the claim holder keeps the key throughout.

scenes.title: The Comb
paragraphs: *Oss Station, observation ring · Hour 0 of 40*

Eleven days out, the comet Maren-Quill had grown a second tail, and the second tail was walking the wrong way. The first streamed from the sun as tails should. The new one crawled up into the solar wind, a thin violet braid shedding knots of charged dust that tumbled across the freight corridor like seeds across a road.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
Those knots are alive, in whatever sense a field can be. They fold dust into shells, and inside each shell something keeps a heartbeat on the low radio band. Nine thousand shells, all young. And every shell scatters our navigation. A ranging beam comes out of that braid like light through frosted glass.

**Ngozi Farrant**  
Ardent has a fix good to eighty metres, when the lane needs four. I carry nineteen hundred tonnes of grain, and my radiation margin lets me reroute exactly never.

**Ibrahim Tadesse**  
Lamentine's mills turn for eleven more days. The other four stations are not far behind. The lane closes for the perihelion in forty hours. Three convoys must cross before then, or my people eat the seed stock.

**Dagny Voss, on the line**  
And the comet is mine, Councillor, under the Voss-Kane charter, down to the last gram of nickel. The charter lets a holder clear a hazard to navigation from her own claim. At Hour 12 I fire the comb. Forty minutes, and the lane is clean as glass.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
And so is the nursery. A magnetic sweep tears every shell apart.

**Dagny Voss, on the line**  
I read your paper, doctor. A pretty braid. Four hundred people draw wages from this claim, and they will not draw them from a braid.
Illuminara had stood at the window the whole time, watching the violet thread on the screen below the stars. Nobody had asked her opinion yet. She did not offer one.

**Illuminara**  
Not the summary. The raw tracks. Every knot, every minute since the braid formed.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
That is two terabytes of scribble.

**Illuminara**  
Then nobody has read it yet.

scenes.title: The Beacon That Lost Its Clock
paragraphs: *Oss Station, tracking bay · Hour 3*
She read the tracks the way she read a face, looking for the place where the expected thing failed to happen. It took her an hour and ten minutes. She found it in a gap forty minutes wide.

**Illuminara**  
Beacon nine lost its clock at 22:10 yesterday. Its phase wandered for forty minutes. Look at the knots in that stretch.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
They parted. Around the beacon, in a bubble. I took it for a sensor fault.

**Illuminara**  
They parted for exactly forty minutes and closed the moment the clock came back. You told the council the knots hunt the beams. A thing hunting beams would have swarmed the one that was shouting.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
Unless they shun anything incoherent.

**Illuminara**  
And they are not drifting at random. Every strand runs along the old guide rails, the magnetic edges laid down to keep the beams clean. The rails are the quietest, straightest edges in forty million kilometres.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
Then we built them a road. And we invited them onto it.

**Ngozi Farrant, on the line**  
Then cut the rails.

**Illuminara**  
Then your ranging goes with them, the lane turns to static, and I do not know what a young shell does when its road becomes noise.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
Fracture. I would guess.

**Illuminara**  
It is a guess, and I would rather not learn the answer by being right. Suppose we offered something quieter, longer and cleaner than the rails, and led away from traffic.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
You are assuming they take offers.

**Illuminara**  
I am assuming nothing. I want to see whether they decline.

scenes.title: The Key
paragraphs: *Voss-Kane platform, comb control · Hour 6*
Dagny Voss kept the firing key on a cord around her own neck. Her engineer, Kemal Aydin, stood at the panel with his hands in his pockets, which Illuminara understood to be a courtesy.

**Dagny Voss**  
You have come to ask me to wait.

**Illuminara**  
I have come to ask what would make you not fire.

**Dagny Voss**  
A clean lane before Hour 12. Show me ranging lock to four metres, and I will not touch the key. I will also want to see the thing I am sparing. I do not break my own payroll over a diagram.

**Illuminara**  
Then take the heartbeat. Dr. Achterberg can put it on this panel. While the shells are whole it is a single clean note. If they tear, it spreads into static. You will watch harm happen the moment it does, and you can fire the second you see it.

**Kemal Aydin**  
Which means you are handing her the right to stop you.

**Illuminara**  
It was always hers.

**Dagny Voss**  
And if you are wrong, I want it on the record that I warned you, and that every hour I waited cost me a hauler contract.

**Illuminara**  
It will be on the record. The cost will be too.

**Dagny Voss**  
Then do it. Hour 12 is when Kemal turns the comb. I will wait past it for as long as the lane is getting better and the heartbeat stays whole. The first time either one turns, he fires, and I will not be asked twice.

scenes.title: Two Ribbons
paragraphs: *Oss and Lamentine field arrays · Hour 8 to Hour 10 and a half*

The first ribbon ran out from Oss, south and away from the lane: a faint coherent edge, drawn as cleanly as the arrays could draw it. The second ran from Lamentine across the corridor, a decoy and a control. Illuminara wrote her prediction in the station log before either went live. The knots would leave the rails for the outbound ribbon within ninety minutes. If they took neither, or the crossing one, she was wrong, and she wrote that too.
They did nothing for seventy minutes. On Voss's panel the heartbeat held one clean note, and Aydin counted the minutes aloud in a flat voice.

At 09:20 the knots moved. They did not take the outbound ribbon, and they did not take the crossing one. They settled on the seam where the two edges overlapped, a line nobody had drawn, running a hundred and forty kilometres along the lane's southern rail.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
They declined both.

**Illuminara**  
No. They chose the best edge in the sky, and I built it by accident. I had them picking between my offers.

**Ngozi Farrant, on the line**  
My fix just went to a hundred and twenty metres. Tell me that is the end of the bad news.

**Illuminara**  
It is the middle. I made the lane worse.
She said it once, at the volume she would have used for a measurement, and went back to the screen. It was 10:35.

scenes.title: The Seam
paragraphs: *Oss field array, control room · Hour 10 and 40 minutes*

**Illuminara**  
The seam sits where the two ribbons are equal. Weaken the crossing one and the seam slides toward Lamentine's side, away from the rail. Strengthen the outbound one and it slides the same way. Slide it slowly and the knots may follow it, because it is still the best edge there is.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
The arrays can't hold their phase that precisely. They wander. Noise is exactly what the knots flee.

**Illuminara**  
Then I will be the clock. I can feel which way each field is bending a breath before your instruments log it. I cannot move the knots, or the ice, or the shells. I can tell each of you which way you are drifting and by how much.

**Ibrahim Tadesse**  
Lamentine's array runs on the mill reserve. Drain it for this and the mill stays cold a day. Four thousand households will go without bread.

**Illuminara**  
I will not pretend that is a small price.

**Ibrahim Tadesse**  
Take it.

For forty minutes she called corrections over two channels, one voice to Oss and one to Lamentine, a few milliseconds ahead of what the instruments could see. The seam crept south. The knots flowed along it like seeds along a tide line.
At minute forty-one Voss's voice came over the speaker, level and dry.

**Dagny Voss, on the line**  
The heartbeat is broadening.
Illuminara did not argue the point. She said stop, and she held the arrays exactly where they were. Aydin's hand was on the comb, and no one in the room breathed.

**Dagny Voss, on the line**  
Tell me why I should not turn it.

**Illuminara**  
Because the pull outran the young. The elders came with the seam and the youngest could not keep the pace, and you are looking at the shells stretching. I should have set the slope slower. Give me twenty minutes of stillness. If the note does not narrow, turn the key.
For twenty minutes the seam did not move and the heartbeat did not settle, and then, a little at a time, it did. The laggards were catching up, and the braid closed behind them like a hand.

**Dagny Voss, on the line**  
Resume. Half the speed.

scenes.title: Clean Glass
paragraphs: *Oss Station and the lane · Hour 16 to Hour 31*

By Hour 15 the seam lay two hundred kilometres south of the rail, and the braid lay with it, a long violet comma pointing away from the lane. Ranging lock came back in steps: eighty metres, forty, nine, four.

**Ngozi Farrant**  
Four. Four and holding. I said I would not enter above eighty metres, and I am entering at four on my own judgement, not because anyone told me it was safe. Ardent is in the lane.

Illuminara watched the scatter chart flatten on Oss's screen. The three convoys crossed one behind another, at half speed, through the narrow clean band, and the last of them cleared the closing line with nine hours to spare. The grain would reach the stations two days late. The mills of Lamentine would burn their reserves and turn again only when the first loaves arrived.
Voss came to the observation ring herself, with the key on its cord.

**Dagny Voss**  
A season. The north face is still mine, but the south face is shut while the heartbeat band is active, and the charter will say so in writing. I have never signed away a season for a diagram.

**Illuminara**  
It stopped being a diagram when you could hear it.

**Ibrahim Tadesse**  
The new beacons will be paid for by every hauler on the lane. Nobody has agreed to that yet.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
They will have to. The next braid will not wait for a committee.

On the screen the heartbeat held its single clean note, and under it, new and faint, a second tone that had not been there before. Achterberg turned it up. Nobody could say what it meant, and Illuminara did not offer a guess. She asked, instead, that one ribbon be left on at a whisper through the season, and Voss, after a moment, nodded.

scenes.title: The Seam
paragraphs: *Oss field array, control room · Hour 10 and 40 minutes*

The seam sits where the two ribbons are equal. Weaken the crossing one and strengthen the outbound one by the same amount, and the seam slides south without becoming brighter. Slide it slowly and the knots may follow it, because it remains coherent.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
Or charged dust is simply collecting where the fields cancel. Then coherence has nothing to do with it.

**Kemal Aydin, on the line**  
I can rotate both phases equally and oppositely for forty seconds. The seam stays within two kilometres and total field strength within one percent, but the edge loses coherence. If the knots follow strength or geometry, they stay. If they follow coherence, their track should loosen before the six-minute mark.

**Illuminara**  
Freeze that prediction in the log. Forty seconds only. If the heartbeat widens by more than five percent, restore phase at once. If their track does not loosen within six minutes, my model fails and we do not begin the slide.

At Hour 10:47 Aydin rotated the phases. The seam did not move on the ranging plot. Seventy seconds later the outer knots lifted from it and began to wander, though the heartbeat remained narrow. He restored coherence at forty seconds; within four minutes the same knots had gathered along the seam again. They had not chosen either ribbon. They had answered a property of the edge.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
That defeats accumulation. It does not prove what they are, but it tells us what not to break.

**Illuminara**  
Then we move only one thing: the position of a coherent seam.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
The arrays cannot hold their phase that precisely. They wander. Noise is exactly what the knots flee.

**Illuminara**  
Then I will be the clock. I can feel which way each field is bending a breath before your instruments log it. I cannot move the knots, or the dust, or the shells. I can tell each of you which way you are drifting and by how much.

**Ibrahim Tadesse**  
Lamentine has eleven days of grain in sealed silos, but only fourteen hours of bread already baked. The mill reserve keeps the grinders and ovens alive through a brownout. Give it to the array and the mill stays cold until we release the field power. Households eat yesterday's loaves, and the outer stations still need these convoys.

**Illuminara**  
I will not pretend that is a small price.

**Ibrahim Tadesse**  
I authorize fourteen hours. The mill restarts the moment the array releases the reserve. Take it.

At Hour 11:00 she began calling corrections over two channels, one voice to Oss and one to Lamentine, a few milliseconds ahead of what the instruments could see. The seam crept south. The knots flowed along it like seeds along a tide line.
At Hour 11:41 Voss's voice came over the speaker, level and dry.

**Dagny Voss, on the line**  
The heartbeat is twelve percent broader. My condition was whole, not almost whole. Aydin has his hand on the comb.
Illuminara did not argue. She ordered the arrays held exactly where they were.

**Illuminara**  
The pull outran the young. The elders came with the seam and the youngest could not keep the pace. I set the slope too fast. Give me until Hour 12:05 with the seam still. If the width is not within five percent of its starting line, turn the key. If it recovers, grant twenty minutes at half speed. Renew only while two ten-minute reads show the width holding and the ranging error falling.

**Dagny Voss, on the line**  
That is the bargain. Five percent by 12:05. After that, twenty minutes at a time. One bad pair of reads and Kemal fires without another speech.
At Hour 12:01 the heartbeat narrowed to four percent above its starting width. Aydin read the number himself. The laggards had caught up, and the braid closed behind them like a hand.

**Kemal Aydin, on the line**  
Four percent. Ranging error is falling. The condition is met.

**Dagny Voss, on the line**  
Resume. Half the speed. Your window ends at 12:21 unless the next pair earns another.

paragraphs: *Oss Station and the lane · Hour 15 to Hour 31*

By Hour 15 the seam lay two hundred kilometres south of the rail, and the braid lay with it, a long violet comma pointing away from the lane. Voss renewed the twenty-minute window seven times, each time after Aydin read two improving fixes and a heartbeat no more than five percent wide. Ranging lock came back in steps: eighty metres, forty, nine, four.

Four. Four and holding. I said I would not enter above eighty metres, and I am entering at four on my own judgement, not because anyone told me it was safe. Ardent is in the lane.

**Dagny Voss**  
A season. The north face remains mine, but I surrender extraction on the south face while the heartbeat band is active. That cost is mine, and the charter will say so in writing.

**Ibrahim Tadesse, on the line**  
Oss Council declares the same band a protected navigation exclusion through perihelion. Voss-Kane's assent and the public order expire together at the season's end unless both are renewed.

**Illuminara**  
It stopped being a diagram when each of you could measure what your choice would harm.

**Ibrahim Tadesse, on the line**  
The new beacons will be paid for by every hauler on the lane. Nobody has agreed to that yet.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
Then that argument begins tomorrow. The next braid will not wait for us to finish it.

Nobody could say what it meant, and Illuminara did not offer a guess. She asked, instead, that one ribbon be left on at a whisper through the season. Voss looked once at Aydin's trace, then nodded.

The second ran from Lamentine across the corridor, a decoy and a control. Illuminara wrote her prediction in the station log before either went live. The knots would leave the rails for the outbound ribbon within ninety minutes. If they took neither, or the crossing one, she was wrong, and she wrote that too.
They did nothing for seventy minutes. On Voss's panel the heartbeat held one clean note, and Aydin counted the minutes aloud in a flat voice.

At Hour 9:20 the knots moved. They did not take the outbound ribbon, and they did not take the crossing one. They settled on the seam where the two edges overlapped, a line nobody had drawn, running a hundred and forty kilometres along the lane's southern rail.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
They declined both.

**Illuminara**  
No. They chose the best edge in the sky, and I built it by accident. I had them picking between my offers.

**Ngozi Farrant, on the line**  
My fix just went to a hundred and twenty metres. Tell me that is the end of the bad news.

**Illuminara**  
It is the middle. I made the lane worse.
She said it once, at the volume she would have used for a measurement, and went back to the screen. It was Hour 10:35.

scenes.title: The Seam
paragraphs: *Oss field array, control room · Hour 10:40*

**Illuminara**  
The seam sits where the two ribbons are equal. Weaken the crossing one and strengthen the outbound one by the same amount, and the seam slides south without becoming brighter. Slide it slowly and the knots may follow it, because it remains coherent.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
Or charged dust is simply collecting where the fields cancel. Then coherence has nothing to do with it.

**Kemal Aydin, on the line**  
I can rotate both phases equally and oppositely for forty seconds. The seam stays within two kilometres and total field strength within one percent, but the edge loses coherence. If the knots follow strength or geometry, they stay. If they follow coherence, their track should loosen before the six-minute mark.

**Illuminara**  
Freeze that prediction in the log. Forty seconds only. If the heartbeat widens by more than five percent, restore phase at once. If their track does not loosen within six minutes, my model fails and we do not begin the slide.

At Hour 10:47 Aydin rotated the phases. The seam did not move on the ranging plot. Seventy seconds later the outer knots lifted from it and began to wander, though the heartbeat remained narrow. He restored coherence at forty seconds; within four minutes the same knots had gathered along the seam again. They had not chosen either ribbon. They had answered a property of the edge.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
That defeats accumulation. It does not prove what they are, but it tells us what not to break.

**Illuminara**  
Then we move only one thing: the position of a coherent seam.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
The arrays cannot hold their phase that precisely. They wander. Noise is exactly what the knots flee.

**Illuminara**  
Then I will be the clock. I can feel which way each field is bending a breath before your instruments log it. I cannot move the knots, or the dust, or the shells. I can tell each of you which way you are drifting and by how much.

**Ibrahim Tadesse**  
Lamentine has eleven days of grain in sealed silos, but only fourteen hours of bread already baked. The mill reserve keeps the grinders and ovens alive through a brownout. Give it to the array and the mill stays cold until we release the field power. Households eat yesterday's loaves, and the outer stations still need these convoys.

**Illuminara**  
I will not pretend that is a small price.

**Ibrahim Tadesse**  
I authorize fourteen hours. The mill restarts the moment the array releases the reserve. Take it.

At Hour 11:00 she began calling corrections over two channels, one voice to Oss and one to Lamentine. At Hour 11:06 she called Oss drifting 0.18 degrees sunward; the instrument alarm crossed the same threshold 3.2 seconds later, and Aydin entered both times in Voss's log.

At Hour 11:29 Lamentine stepped against her call. This time the array alarm sounded 0.6 seconds before she corrected it. The outermost shells loosened for eleven seconds before the seam recovered. Her lead was real, and it was not constant enough to make the ecology safe by itself.
The seam crept south. The knots flowed along it like seeds along a tide line.
At Hour 11:41 Voss's voice came over the speaker, level and dry.

**Dagny Voss, on the line**  
The heartbeat is twelve percent broader. My line was five. Aydin has his hand on the comb.
Illuminara did not argue. She ordered the arrays held exactly where they were.

**Illuminara**  
The pull outran the young. The older keepers came with the seam and the newest shells could not keep the pace. I set the slope too fast. Give me until Hour 12:05 with the seam still. If the width is not within five percent of its starting line, turn the key. If it recovers, grant twenty minutes at half speed. Renew only while two ten-minute reads show the width holding and the ranging error falling.

**Dagny Voss, on the line**  
That is the recovery window. Five percent by Hour 12:05. After that, twenty minutes at a time. One bad pair of reads and Kemal fires without another speech.
At Hour 12:01 the heartbeat narrowed to four percent above its starting width. Aydin read the number himself. The laggards had caught up, and the braid closed behind them like a hand.

**Kemal Aydin, on the line**  
Four percent. Ranging error is falling. The condition is met.

**Dagny Voss, on the line**  
Resume. Half the speed. Your window ends at Hour 12:21 unless the next pair earns another.

scenes.title: Clean Glass
paragraphs: *Oss Station and the lane · Hour 15 to Hour 31*

By Hour 15 the seam lay two hundred kilometres south of the rail, and the braid lay with it, a long violet comma pointing away from the lane. Voss renewed the twenty-minute window seven times, each time after Aydin read two improving fixes and a heartbeat no more than five percent wide. Ranging lock came back in steps: eighty metres, forty, nine, four.

Beyond the ribbons' crossing point, the comet's own southward field gradient ran parallel to the Oss outbound ribbon. Together they made the sole quiet edge; Lamentine's crossing array no longer set the seam's position. Aydin reduced that array in three logged steps, and the braid did not move or widen.

**Ngozi Farrant**  
Four. Four and holding. I said I would not enter above eighty metres, and I am entering at four on my own judgement, not because anyone told me it was safe. Ardent is in the lane.

Illuminara watched the scatter chart flatten on Oss's screen. The three convoys crossed one behind another, at half speed, through the narrow clean band, and the last cleared the closing line with nine hours to spare. Lamentine released its array at Hour 15:12 after the third stable step; the Oss ribbon and the comet's gradient held the braid on the new edge. The mill restarted on stored grain before the fourteen-hour bread shelf was empty. The convoys would reach the stations two days behind schedule; Pelion and Kestrel would receive them before either opened its seed stores.
Voss came to the observation ring herself, with the key on its cord. Tadesse joined by public line, carrying Oss Council's emergency navigation seal.

**Dagny Voss**  
A season. The north face remains mine, but I surrender extraction on the south face while the heartbeat band is active. That cost is mine, and the charter will say so in writing.

**Ibrahim Tadesse, on the line**  
Oss Council declares the same band a protected navigation exclusion through perihelion. Voss-Kane's assent and the public order expire together at the season's end unless both are renewed.

**Illuminara**  
It stopped being a diagram when each of you could measure what your choice would harm.

**Ibrahim Tadesse, on the line**  
The new beacons will be paid for by every hauler on the lane. Nobody has agreed to that yet.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
Then that argument begins tomorrow. The next braid will not wait for us to finish it.

On the screen the heartbeat held its single clean note, and under it, new and faint, a second tone that had not been there before. Achterberg turned it up. Nobody could say what it meant, and Illuminara did not offer a guess. She asked, instead, that one ribbon be left on at a whisper through the season. Voss looked once at Aydin's trace, then nodded.

story.title: THE COMET'S SECOND TAIL
story.deck: A comet grows a tail that walks upwind, nine thousand young shells of living plasma sit across the grain lane, and a claim holder keeps the key to a sweep that would sterilize them.
story.shape: Interplanetary corridor crisis in six scenes: the ecology declines both offered paths, chooses a third, and has to be met at its own pace; the claim holder keeps the key throughout.

scenes.title: The Comb
paragraphs: *Oss Station, observation ring · Hour 0 of 40*

Eleven days out, the comet Maren-Quill had grown a second tail, and the second tail was walking the wrong way. The first streamed from the sun as tails should. The new one crawled up into the solar wind, a thin violet braid shedding knots of charged dust that tumbled across the freight corridor like seeds across a road.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
Those knots are alive, in whatever sense a field can be. They fold dust into shells, and inside each shell something keeps a heartbeat on the low radio band. Nine thousand shells, mostly young, but their pulse bands show older keepers around the outer edge and newly folded shells inside. I told the council the knots are drawn to our ranging beams: every shell scatters our navigation. A beam comes out of that braid like light through frosted glass.

**Ibrahim Tadesse**  
Lamentine's sealed silos can feed its mills for eleven days, but Pelion has three days of grain and Kestrel two. The lane closes at perihelion in forty hours and stays closed six weeks. Ardent and the two other convoys must cross before then, or the outer stations eat seed stock before the next window.

**Dagny Voss, on the line**  
And the comet is mine, Councillor, under the Voss-Kane charter, down to the last gram of nickel. The charter lets a holder clear a hazard to navigation from her own claim. At Hour 12 I fire the comb. Forty minutes, and the lane is clean as glass.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
And so is the nursery. A magnetic sweep tears every shell apart.

**Dagny Voss, on the line**  
I read your paper, doctor. A pretty braid. Four hundred people draw wages from this claim, and they will not draw them from a braid.
Illuminara had stood at the window the whole time, watching the violet thread on the screen below the stars. Nobody had asked her opinion yet. She did not offer one.

**Illuminara**  
Not the summary. The raw tracks. Every knot, every minute since the braid formed.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
That is two terabytes of scribble.

**Illuminara**  
Then nobody has read it yet.

scenes.title: The Beacon That Lost Its Clock
paragraphs: *Oss Station, tracking bay · Hour 3*
She read the tracks the way she read a face, looking for the place where the expected thing failed to happen. It took her an hour and ten minutes. She found it in a gap forty minutes wide.
When the replay reached the fault, Illuminara named a 0.04-degree phase wobble 2.1 seconds before the instrument flag; the tracking technician checked the log and confirmed the lead.

**Illuminara**  
Beacon nine lost its clock at 22:10 yesterday — wall-clock time, before our forty-hour count began. Its phase wandered for forty minutes. Look at the knots in that stretch.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
They parted. Around the beacon, in a bubble. I took it for a sensor fault.

**Illuminara**  
They parted for exactly forty minutes and closed the moment the clock came back. You told the council the knots hunt the beams. A thing hunting beams would have swarmed the one that was shouting.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
Unless they shun anything incoherent.

**Illuminara**  
And they are not drifting at random. Every strand runs along the old guide rails, the magnetic edges laid down to keep the beams clean. The rails are the quietest, straightest edges in forty million kilometres.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
Then we built them a road. And we invited them onto it.

**Ngozi Farrant, on the line**  
Then cut the rails.

**Illuminara**  
Then your ranging goes with them, the lane turns to static, and I do not know what a young shell does when its road becomes noise.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
Fracture. I would guess.

**Illuminara**  
It is a guess, and I would rather not learn the answer by being right. Suppose we offered something quieter, longer and cleaner than the rails, and led away from traffic.

**Sunniva Achterberg**  
You are assuming they take offers.

**Illuminara**  
I am assuming nothing. I want to see whether they decline.

scenes.title: The Key
paragraphs: *Voss-Kane platform, comb control · Hour 6*
Dagny Voss kept the firing key on a cord around her own neck. Her engineer, Kemal Aydin, stood at the panel with his hands in his pockets, which Illuminara understood to be a courtesy.

**Dagny Voss**  
You have come to ask me to wait.

**Illuminara**  
I have come to ask what would make you not fire.

**Dagny Voss**  
A clean lane before Hour 12. Show me ranging lock to four metres, and I will not touch the key. I will also want to see the thing I am sparing. I do not break my own payroll over a diagram.

**Illuminara**  
Then take the heartbeat. Dr. Achterberg can put it on this panel. While the shells are whole it is a single clean note. We will log its starting width. If the note widens by more than five percent, the shells are falling out of step and the test has breached its limit.

**Kemal Aydin**  
Which means you are handing her the right to stop you.

**Illuminara**  
It was always hers.

**Dagny Voss**  
And if you are wrong, I want it on the record that I warned you, and that every hour I waited cost me a hauler contract.

**Illuminara**  
It will be on the record. The cost will be too.

**Dagny Voss**  
Then do it. At Hour 12 Kemal turns the comb unless the lane is improving and that note is within five percent of its starting width. If either measure turns against you, he holds the fields where they are and I decide whether you get one recovery window or the comb. I will not be asked twice.
